chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Muhammad) from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah from Al-Hadrami from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman while he already has a wife. He said: 'If she is a virgin, he should spend the night with her for seven days; and if she is a non-virgin, for three days.'

This report does not contradict the previously mentioned reports, because we interpret the first reports as meaning that he is permitted to prefer the virgin by three days, as she is superior, and then return to equality. And we interpret the last report as indicating permissibility rather than obligation; for whoever does so is not sinful, even if he has left the superior option.

key_terms.بِكْرًا: virgin (a woman who has not been married before)
key_terms.ثَيِّبًا: non-virgin (a woman who has been married before)
key_terms.يُفَضِّلَ: to prefer or give priority to

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended duration for a husband to stay with a new virgin wife versus a non-virgin wife according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a recommended practice (mustahabb) for a husband to prioritize his new wife, granting her exclusive companionship for seven days if she is a virgin or three days if she is a non-virgin. Shia jurists reconcile this with other hadiths by interpreting it as a preferred act of kindness rather than an obligatory duty, meaning the husband incurs no sin if he chooses to equalize his time with all wives immediately after the marriage contract.
